title: The Deputy Takes Dictation
bold_reframe: Prompt injection isn't an input-filtering bug; it's the confused deputy problem from 1988. The fix is the same: give the agent less authority, not better instructions.

title: Same Weights, Worse Answers
bold_reframe: Model quality is an infrastructure SLO. The weights didn't change; the serving stack did. If your evals only run before deploy, you can't see the failures that actually ship.

title: The File That Fit Yesterday
bold_reframe: Generated config is a deploy that skips your deploy pipeline. If a file can take down production, it needs the same canary, validation and rollback as code.

title: The Context Window Is a Cache
bold_reframe: The context window isn't a prompt; it's the scarcest tier in your memory hierarchy. Loading every tool definition up front is like copying the whole disk into L1.

title: The Speed You Feel
bold_reframe: AI coding tools are judged by how fast developers feel, not how fast work ships. Until you measure delivery outcomes, your AI rollout runs on vibes, not evidence.

title: Every Span Has a Price
bold_reframe: Telemetry is a product with a unit cost, not a free byproduct. Agents multiply spans per request, so sampling by value is now an architecture decision, not a billing afterthought.

title: Harness Over Horsepower
bold_reframe: In AI systems, the model is a replaceable dependency. The harness — your routing logic, fallback patterns, cost controls, and reliability layer — is the actual product.

title: Guarding the Garden
bold_reframe: Paved paths don't scale to autonomous agents; we need guard-railed gardens where the AI can explore dynamically but the infrastructure constrains the blast radius.

title: The Paved Path Paradox
bold_reframe: Standardization doesn't eliminate risk; it concentrates it into a single, catastrophic blast radius. True platform reliability comes from controlled flexibility, not rigid uniformity.

title: The Drift You Can't See
bold_reframe: Your AI observability stack is watching the infrastructure, not the intelligence.

title: Crying Wolf in Code
bold_reframe: AI observability alerts on the wrong signal because we measure plumbing instead of water quality.

title: Mind the Gap
bold_reframe: Direct — AI observability fails because we monitor the plumbing (HTTP 200s) instead of the water (semantic success).

title: Guard the Graph
bold_reframe: Your AI agent security model is backwards — you're guarding the prompt when you should be guarding the tool graph. The blast radius isn't what you tell the agent, it's what the agent can reach.

title: Pave, Don't Pick
bold_reframe: Developer platforms that accelerate shipping don't give engineers more choices — they give them fewer decisions.

title: Automating the Outage
bold_reframe: GitOps doesn't prevent outages; it automates them.

title: The Desired State Delusion
bold_reframe: GitOps isn't pulling your infrastructure closer to desired state; it's accelerating drift by treating infrastructure as version-controlled code rather than ephemeral state.

title: Wolves at the Door
bold_reframe: We are building autonomous systems with user-level permissions but API-level oversight, effectively giving them keys to the kingdom and a blindfold.

title: Blind Spots
bold_reframe: Stop monitoring your LLMs like web servers. Agents don't crash; they hallucinate, loop, and confidently fail. A 200 OK is useless if the model is confidently lying. It's time for behavioral observability.

title: The Paved Path Illusion
bold_reframe: Standardization isn't about building paved paths; it's about eradicating the off-ramps.

title: Paved With Good Intentions
bold_reframe: A paved path is a toll road. If you don't enforce the toll, you're just paving a dirt road in a swamp.

title: Paving Over the Portal
bold_reframe: The developer portal is the new ticket queue — real enablement means engineers never visit your platform UI; the most productive platform teams build pavement that disappears into existing workflows.

title: The Tail Wags the Model
bold_reframe: The model is the least important part of your AI architecture; the routing harness dictates whether you scale or collapse.

title: Automating the Wrong Thing
bold_reframe: GitOps doesn't prevent outages; it just automates how fast you can break everything.

title: Handing Over the Keys
bold_reframe: We are treating AI agent permissions as static IAM roles, when they actually need dynamic, session-scoped, intent-based authorization.

title: Blind Spots Bleed Black
bold_reframe: AI observability isn't about tracing what the model did; it's about observing what the harness allowed it to do.

title: Now You Don't
bold_reframe: Your developer platform isn't failing because it lacks features — it's failing because engineers have to go to it. The best platform is the one nobody visits.

title: The Routing Robin Hood
bold_reframe: Your AI model router is not a load balancer; it is a high-frequency trading engine, and treating it like one is the only way to survive inference costs.

title: The Automation Trap
bold_reframe: GitOps doesn't prevent outages; it automates them. Reconciliation loops are not safety nets, but highly efficient outage engines requiring strict rate-limiting.

title: Blind Spots, Bright Logs
bold_reframe: Your AI agent's audit trail is a lie — not because the logs are wrong, but because they attribute every action to the human user, even when the true author was a prompt injected by a third party.
